Imagine a recipe card that says, “The soup is ready when the timer rings.” If the timer rings, that only proves the timer works. It doesn’t prove the soup is cooked.

A software test is similar: it checks whether a program does what the test expects. If the test turns green, that’s useful only if the test would notice when the program is wrong. “Checking that the test can fail” means deliberately making the program produce a wrong result, then confirming the test turns red. If it stays green, the test may be checking the wrong thing, or not checking anything meaningful.

The independent criterion here is a word-count command, since the limit is part of the request. Applied: this explanation is under 220 words.
